title: Insights into the aetiology of snoring from observational and genetic investigations in the UK Biobank
primary_finding: Supplementary Data 2 directly reported a negative snoring correlation with parents age at death.
limitations: Not independent of the atlas snoring GWAS; external source definition and cohort cannot be treated as exact independent replication; nominal P=0.0432.

title: Insights into the aetiology of snoring from observational and genetic investigations in the UK Biobank
primary_finding: The snoring paper prioritized loci and regulatory annotations across several tissues.
limitations: Trait-only annotation cannot establish a snoring-parental-lifespan locus, shared signal, gene, tissue, or cell mechanism.

title: Genomics of 1 million parent lifespans implicates novel pathways and common diseases and distinguishes survival chances
primary_finding: Large parental-lifespan GWAS supplies the atlas external phenotype.
limitations: Discovery source, not replication and not an exact pairwise mechanistic study.

title: A Prospective Analysis of Genetic Variants Associated with Human Lifespan
primary_finding: AncestryDNA discovery exceeded 300,000 participants; a later meta-analysis included an independent UK Biobank dataset.
limitations: The independent AncestryDNA component is not an analysis-ready public full summary-statistics release identified by this audit; the meta-analysis is not independent of UKB.

title: Genome-wide Association Study of Parental Life Span
primary_finding: HRS-based parental longevity analysis provides an independently sampled, related phenotype.
limitations: Small and phenotype definition differs; the top signal did not provide a well-powered exact pair replication and no public dense signed release was identified.

title: No exact mechanistic paper identified in targeted search
primary_finding: No exact snoring-parental-lifespan local, signal-aware, cellular, chromatin, or spatial analysis was identified.
limitations: A targeted search cannot prove absence; indexing, terminology, and unpublished work remain limitations.

title: Sleep-related traits and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder comorbidity: Shared genetic risk factors, molecular mechanisms, and causal effects
primary_finding: Directly reported a positive genomic correlation between insomnia and ADHD.
limitations: Uses earlier/largely overlapping public GWAS families and is prior evidence, not independent Track B replication.

method: gene-based cross-trait meta-analysis; enrichment; two-sample MR
title: Sleep-related traits and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder comorbidity: Shared genetic risk factors, molecular mechanisms, and causal effects
primary_finding: Reported shared genes/pathways and MR evidence for sleep traits and ADHD.
limitations: Gene-based overlap is not fine-mapping or trait-trait colocalization; MR is vulnerable to pleiotropy and does not prove mediation.

title: Genome-wide analyses of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder identify 27 risk loci, refine the genetic architecture, and implicate several cognitive domains
primary_finding: The ADHD discovery paper included insomnia among genetically correlated phenotypes.
limitations: It uses the exact atlas ADHD source and therefore cannot provide independent replication.

title: Detection of pleiotropic genetic factors and critical brain cell types linking insomnia with psychiatric disorders
primary_finding: Insomnia showed significant genetic correlation with ADHD and six other psychiatric disorders.
limitations: Transdiagnostic design and overlapping GWAS sources limit pair-specific novelty and independence.

title: Detection of pleiotropic genetic factors and critical brain cell types linking insomnia with psychiatric disorders
primary_finding: Across insomnia and psychiatric disorders, 70 shared loci were reported; seven novel associations were assigned to ADHD.
limitations: Shared-locus methods do not by themselves establish a single shared causal variant or mediation.

title: Detection of pleiotropic genetic factors and critical brain cell types linking insomnia with psychiatric disorders
primary_finding: Four GABAergic and four glutamatergic cortical neuron subtypes were implicated across the insomnia-psychiatric analysis.
limitations: Abstract-level evidence does not establish that every subtype is ADHD-specific; enrichment is not cell-specific eQTL colocalization.

title: Detection of pleiotropic genetic factors and critical brain cell types linking insomnia with psychiatric disorders
primary_finding: The study supports cortical GABA/glutamate involvement in the broader insomnia-psychiatric architecture.
limitations: A headline ADHD-specific subtype claim requires inspection/replication of pair-specific results, not extrapolation from the aggregate abstract.

title: Dynamic relationship and pleiotropic loci of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder with sleep traits
primary_finding: Reported strong positive ADHD-insomnia genetic correlation in an exploratory adult UKB insomnia analysis.
limitations: Adult result was an adjunct to pediatric ABCD analyses and has substantial source overlap with the atlas.

title: Dynamic relationship and pleiotropic loci of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder with sleep traits
primary_finding: PLACO identified 14 lead SNPs across 12 insomnia-ADHD risk loci.
limitations: PLACO is statistical pleiotropy; clumping and gene mapping do not establish biological mediation.

title: Dynamic relationship and pleiotropic loci of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder with sleep traits
primary_finding: Four loci exceeded PP4 0.90, including signals near/in FOXP2, LSAMP, PTPRD and lincRNA RP11-6N13.1.
limitations: No signal-aware fine-mapping or prior-sensitivity evidence was identified in the main text; PP4 supports a shared signal but not causality.

method: MAGMA; WebCSEA; Lake et al single-cell enrichment
title: Dynamic relationship and pleiotropic loci of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder with sleep traits
primary_finding: Mapped genes were enriched in brain tissue and neuronal cell populations; pooled ADHD-sleep genes also implicated one microglial cell type.
limitations: Gene-set enrichment is not independent cell-atlas replication or three-way GWAS-GWAS-cell-QTL colocalization.

title: Decoupling Sleep and Brain Size in Childhood: An Investigation of Genetic Covariation in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
primary_finding: Childhood insomnia showed significant genetic covariance with ADHD/externalizing symptoms in ABCD.
limitations: N approximately 4,700, dimensional childhood traits, and different estimator/phenotype prevent use as standardized independent LDSC replication.

method: cell-specific eQTL/sQTL coloc; scATAC; spatial transcriptomics search
title: No exact convergent cell-QTL/chromatin/spatial report identified
primary_finding: No exact insomnia-ADHD report was identified that joined trait-trait fine-mapping with cell-specific QTL and same-cell chromatin plus spatial validation.
limitations: Targeted search cannot prove absence; recent and unpublished studies may not be indexed.

title: Investigating the shared genetic architecture between frailty and insomnia
primary_finding: Directly reported strong positive global genetic correlation between insomnia and frailty.
limitations: Both GWAS contain UKB participants; unconstrained rg above one is a warning, and constrained-intercept sensitivity is not a substitute for independent replication.

title: Investigating the shared genetic architecture between frailty and insomnia
primary_finding: A Bonferroni-significant local correlation was reported at 3p21.31.
limitations: rho-HESS/1000 Genomes result should be independently reproduced with the Track B method/reference and scrutinized for local h2 and overlap.

title: Investigating the shared genetic architecture between frailty and insomnia
primary_finding: Cross-trait analyses highlighted shared risk SNPs including rs34290943 and rs10865954.
limitations: Cross-trait association is not fine-mapping or signal-aware trait colocalization.

title: Investigating the shared genetic architecture between frailty and insomnia
primary_finding: Jointly associated SNPs were enriched in multiple brain regions in tissue-level analyses.
limitations: Broad tissue enrichment is not a cell mechanism and may reflect generic expression/annotation architecture.

method: SMR with GTEx eQTL and HEIDI
title: Investigating the shared genetic architecture between frailty and insomnia
primary_finding: SMR/HEIDI highlighted four reported functional genes in enriched tissues.
limitations: Bulk-tissue SMR is not pairwise three-way colocalization and does not establish a mediator.

title: Investigating the shared genetic architecture between frailty and insomnia
primary_finding: The paper reported bidirectional MR evidence.
limitations: Sample overlap and horizontal pleiotropy remain plausible; MR cannot rescue contradictory local/coloc evidence.

title: No exact deep cell-resolved control analysis identified
primary_finding: The known control has global/local/shared-locus/tissue/MR evidence, but no exact signal-aware and cell-resolved chain was identified.
limitations: Targeted search cannot prove absence; the control is intended for concordance, not novelty.
